title: Cursor operating card
summary: For intermediate practitioners, this reference explains why the operating guidance cannot yet be corrected safely and what evidence is required before applying an update. Product-specific instructions whose accuracy is UNKNOWN are omitted.
prerequisites: The verbatim existing cursor-operating-card JSON file
The original citation metadata and its previous claims
A current first-party HTTPS source for each affected claim
Access to the catalogue schema and identifier validation

sections.title: Can I rely on this operating card?
paragraphs: No. An intermediate practitioner cannot safely rely on product-specific operating instructions from the supplied evidence. The existing resource body, its source claims, and a verified first-party replacement source were not supplied, so the current behavior, procedures, interface labels, failure conditions, and recovery actions are UNKNOWN and are omitted.

The cited record is content/resources/coding-tools/cursor-operating-card.json. It is a local path with an unregistered publisher and no recorded verification. A local path is not the required public HTTPS source entry. Whether the original source moved, redirected, was replaced, or merely passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Source correction and safe remediation
paragraphs: The source alleged to have changed is the unverified record for content/resources/coding-tools/cursor-operating-card.json. What changed cannot be established because its original title, publisher, HTTPS URL, verification date, supported claims, and replacement destination are missing. The affected guide material is therefore UNKNOWN, and no product-specific correction is asserted.
First, obtain the verbatim existing JSON and its version-control history. If either is unavailable, stop the update and request both rather than reconstructing the guide from its filename.

Second, recover the original citation title, publisher, HTTPS URL, verification date, and claim mapping. If any item cannot be recovered, mark the associated claim UNKNOWN and omit its correction until the record is available.

Third, open a current first-party source and compare its statements with the claims supported by the original citation. If the page does not resolve over HTTPS or its publisher cannot be confirmed, do not register it and request a verified replacement source.

Fourth, change only claims demonstrably affected by that comparison. If affected and unaffected text cannot be separated, stop rather than replacing the body, because a rewrite would destroy the correction-only review history.

Finally, validate the completed file against the platform Resource schema and the shared catalogue. If parsing, schema validation, identifier uniqueness, or catalogue loading fails, revert the proposed file, retain the diagnostic output, and correct the reported failure before publication.
sections.callout: No existing guide material can be classified reliably as changed or unaffected without the missing baseline. Publication must remain blocked until that evidence is supplied.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A publishable correction must produce a focused version-control diff containing only the source-registration correction and the guide statements demonstrably affected by it. Verify this by comparing the proposed file with the verbatim baseline and confirming that every unrelated field, section, paragraph, procedural step, and configuration reference is unchanged. If unrelated changes appear, revert them before review.

The source record must include a confirmed title, publisher, directly resolving HTTPS URL, and the date on which its contents were actually checked. Verify that the source supports each corrected claim and retain the claim-level comparison. If a claim lacks direct support, mark it UNKNOWN and omit it.

The committed file must parse as one JSON object, conform to the Resource schema, retain exactly three sections, and pass the catalogue uniqueness and loading checks. JSON.parse throws a SyntaxError for text that does not conform to JSON grammar. If any check fails, do not publish; preserve the error output and return the file for correction.
The evidence required to complete this update was not supplied. The expected result is therefore a blocked publication decision, not a claim that the operating guidance is current.
